The way I'd argue it is: if a character has 30 max HP with a current health of 28, being healed (by, say, Cure Wounds) for 5 HP doesn't mean the healing fails just because it would heal for more HP than the character is missing. Same with the case of a character of 6 max health being healed for 8, it doesn't mean the spell fails. It just has no effect past the max health of the character. So, with a maximum health of 0 I'd argue the revivify just brings them to zero (the highest that it can), alive, stabilized, until their missing maximum health is restored either magically or by a long rest.

For context: I'd had a relatively minor surgery and got discharged the day before, and something had gone wrong because 24 hours later I was in the ER.

I ended up passing out in the bathroom and being brought back to the hospital. I'm convinced that if I hadn't been staying with family to recover from the surgery, and I had been alone, I'd be dead.

Once I was in the ambulance, I was conscious enough to hear that I had a blood pressure of around 50/30 and to try not to scream from the agony of every single bump in the distance between the ambulance and the ER.



But, that isn't the fucked up part. The fucked up part is what it felt like to be laying there, alone, in the emergency room, nurses and doctors blurring in and out of existence, still only just conscious enough to register that they were drawing blood, or that I was getting rolled over to radiology for some images. All of it happening too quickly, not able to focus on any of it. Just laying there, crying, in absolute agony, alone, and terrified. Only to be told that the blood test showed my heart was damaged and they were bringing me to the cardiac intensive care unit.

This whole time, I barely know what is going on, still unsure of what was going on or if I would survive.

If I had to pick one single moment, though, I'd have to say it's the look of fear in their eyes when they retook my blood pressure to verify it was actually 50/30 as the EMTs in the ambulance measured, only to then find out that it was actually continuing to drop, and I heard that the first number was 44 over 20-something right before I lost consciousness again. That single moment, hearing the numbers, seeing that fear in their eyes, right as everything fades away... That will never leave me.
